title: The Side Table
subtitle: Six shop techniques, one kitchen side table

chapters.title: Mark Before You Mill
chapters.blurb: Sixteen milled parts that all look alike, and one triangle drawn across a whole group — a mark that means nothing alone and is obviously broken the moment the group goes back wrong.

chapters.title: Wide From Narrow
chapters.blurb: Panels wider than any board you can buy: edge joints, cauls that keep the buckling out of the glue-up, scrap clamping pads, and squeeze-out taken off before it cures to glass.

chapters.title: One Setting, Every Cut
chapters.blurb: Domino joinery run like a sort — group every cut that shares a machine setting, clamp the divider to its panel before mortising, and cut the button slots while the machine is already out.

chapters.title: Square, Round and Flat
chapters.blurb: Diagonals that prove each sub-assembly square, routing the ends before the sides so the tear-out gets cut away, steaming dents up before sanding, and buttons that let the top move.
